steps.title: Start with a criterion
steps.description: What observable result would let you say the work is complete? An intention becomes useful when success can be checked.

steps.title: Choose one bounded action
steps.description: The action has a specific input and an expected outcome. Calling the tool changes what can be observed.

steps.title: Bring evidence back
steps.description: A successful call is evidence about execution. Compare its returned result with the success criterion before claiming completion.

steps.title: Close the reasoning loop
steps.description: Use the result to choose: finish, try another action, or ask for information. Each new action should respond to what was observed.
